text:
Marathon Petroleum stock gained about 1.1% today, bouncing back slightly after a sharp 3.2% drop yesterday. The bounce coincides with oil prices falling as U.S.-Iran peace negotiations resumed, easing fears of supply disruptions in the Middle East — a key driver of crude prices and refiner margins over the past two days. Yesterday's sell-off had come on reports of potential Iran strikes, so the shift toward diplomatic talks removed that immediate supply shock concern.

The stock remains down 9.1% over two weeks, reflecting the whipsaw from geopolitical uncertainty. With U.S. crude around $103 and refineries running at 92.8% capacity, margins depend heavily on oil price stability; the swings between war and peace talk headlines have created real near-term volatility for refining companies.
